versions.statuteQuote: provided that nothing contained in this section shall diminish the duty of the landlord to mitigate actual damages for breach of the rental agreement. In obtaining post-possession judgments for actual damages as defined in this section, the landlord shall not seek a judgment for accelerated rent through the end of the term of the tenancy.

summaryForModel: If the lease ends because the tenant breached it, the landlord can claim rent until the term ends or a new tenant starts, whichever is first, but has a duty to mitigate (try to re-rent). After getting possession, the landlord may not seek a judgment for accelerated rent through the end of the term. A lease that makes all remaining rent due at once, or says the landlord need not try to re-rent, conflicts with this.
paraphraseExamples: If Tenant breaks this Lease, all rent for the remainder of the term becomes immediately due and payable.
Landlord has no obligation to re-rent the Premises if Tenant vacates early.
tenantExplanation: If you move out early, your landlord has to try to rent the place again. They can't get a court judgment for all the rest of your rent at once.
action: You can ask your landlord to remove the clause that makes all remaining rent due at once, or that says they don't have to re-rent.
